learning_outcomes.description: To understand the fundamental principles and concepts of sustainable water infrastructure design.
To explore the different components and elements of water infrastructure systems, including utilities, engineering techniques, and treatment methods.
To analyse and evaluate the performance of existing water infrastructure systems and identify areas for improvement.
To apply sustainable design principles and practices in developing innovative solutions for water infrastructure projects.
To develop critical thinking and problem-solving skills in addressing the challenges and complexities of sustainable water infrastructure design.
To foster an understanding of the social, economic, and environmental impacts of water infrastructure and the importance of sustainability in decision-making.

assessments.task_description:
The In-Semester Examination is an individually verified assessment designed to evaluate students' understanding of the fundamental principles, theories, and analytical methods underpinning sustainable infrastructure design. The examination focuses on the core concepts introduced during the course. Students will be required to demonstrate technical knowledge, interpret engineering scenarios, analyse infrastructure systems, and justify engineering decisions using evidence-based reasoning.

The examination establishes the theoretical foundation for the remainder of the course by ensuring that each student has individually demonstrated competency before progressing to the major design project. Questions will assess students' understanding of engineering principles, their ability to critically analyse existing infrastructure, and their capacity to apply sustainable engineering concepts to realistic scenarios.

This assessment task is to be completed in-person. The use of generative Artificial Intelligence (AI) or Machine Translation (MT) tools will not be permitted. Any attempted use of AI or MT may constitute student misconduct under the Student Code of Conduct.

assessments.task_description:
The Individual Checkpoint is a formative assessment milestone requiring students to submit the preliminary components of their final design project for review and feedback. Students will submit their engineering analysis, infrastructure audit, proposed design methodology, preliminary calculations, and initial sustainable engineering solution. This assessment verifies individual progress, confirms the technical feasibility of the proposed approach, and ensures that students are applying appropriate engineering principles before progressing to the final stage of the project.

Students will be assessed on the quality of their engineering analysis, justification of assumptions, application of sustainable design principles, and their ability to critically evaluate alternative design solutions. Feedback will be provided to strengthen the technical quality of the project and guide further development. Students are expected to incorporate this feedback into their Individual Final Report, demonstrating refinement of their design through critical reflection, technical improvement, and evidence-based engineering judgement.

Students may appropriately use AI and/or MT in completing this assessment task. Students must clearly reference any use of AI or MT in each instance. A failure to reference generative AI or MT use may constitute student misconduct under the Student Code of Conduct.

assessments.task_description:
The Individual Final Report is the capstone assessment for the course and represents the culmination of the semester-long design project. Building on the knowledge demonstrated in the In-Semester Examination and the feedback received during the Individual Checkpoint, students will produce a comprehensive professional engineering report proposing an innovative and sustainable infrastructure solution. The report will demonstrate the complete engineering design process, including technical analysis, design development, sustainability assessment, evaluation of alternative solutions, and evidence-based recommendations.

Students are expected to demonstrate advanced engineering judgement by integrating technical, environmental, economic, and social considerations into a coherent and professionally presented design solution. The report should reflect professional engineering practice through rigorous technical justification, critical evaluation of design decisions, effective communication, and incorporation of feedback received during the checkpoint milestone to demonstrate continuous improvement throughout the design process.

Students may appropriately use AI and/or MT in completing this assessment task. Students must clearly reference any use of AI or MT in each instance. A failure to reference generative AI or MT use may constitute student misconduct under the Student Code of Conduct.
